# Ports, VLANs and Loop Protection

_Extreme Fabric Engine · 48 commands_

Port status, counters and settings, platform VLANs, MAC tables, LLDP, PoE, mirroring and loop protection (SLPP, BPDU Guard).

## Details

### `show interfaces gigabitEthernet name [<ports>]`

```
show interfaces gigabitEthernet name
show interfaces gigabitEthernet name 1/1-1/12
```

The quickest overview of which ports are up. Port lists accept 1/5, 1/1-1/12, 1/1,1/5 and 1/all.


### `show interfaces gigabitEthernet vlan [<ports>]`

Use it when a client lands in the wrong VLAN or tagged frames get dropped.


### `show interfaces gigabitEthernet statistics [<ports>]`

```
show interfaces gigabitEthernet statistics verbose 1/12
```

Add `verbose` for the detailed counters.


### `show interfaces gigabitEthernet error [verbose] [<ports>]`

Clear the counters with `clear-stats port <port>`, then check again to see if errors still increase. Rising CRC errors usually mean a cable, connector or optic problem.


### `clear-stats [port <ports>]`

```
clear-stats port 1/12
```


### `show vlan mac-address-entry [<vid> | mac <mac> | port <ports>]`

```
show vlan mac-address-entry 100
show vlan mac-address-entry mac 00:11:22:33:44:55
show vlan mac-address-entry port 1/5
```

MACs learned across the fabric show the remote BEB (B-MAC/nickname) as the destination instead of a local port.


### `clear mac-address-table port <ports> address <mac> [interface vlan <vid>]`

```
clear mac-address-table port 1/5 address 00:11:22:33:44:55
```


### `interface gigabitEthernet <ports>`

```
interface gigabitEthernet 1/5
interface gigabitEthernet 1/1-1/24,1/48
```


### `name "<description>"`

```
name "AP-2OG-R201"
```


### `no shutdown`

> ▲ **Caution:** `shutdown` on an uplink or NNI cuts off everything behind it.


### `speed <10|100|1000|2500|5000|10000|25000>`

```
no auto-negotiate enable
speed 1000
```

The available speeds depend on the port hardware. A forced speed must match on both sides.

> ▲ **Caution:** The link goes down and comes back up.


### `encapsulation dot1q`

```
interface gigabitEthernet 1/48
encapsulation dot1q
default-vlan-id 100
untag-port-default-vlan enable
```


### `default all [-y | auto-sense]`

```
interface gigabitEthernet 1/5
default all auto-sense
```

The `auto-sense` option was added in 9.3. In 9.2 you had to run `auto-sense enable` afterwards.

> ▲ **Caution:** Removes all VLANs, names and settings from the port.


### `vlan create <vid> name "<name>" type port-mstprstp 0`

```
vlan create 100 name "CLIENTS" type port-mstprstp 0
```

VLAN names cannot be only digits. With the vrf-scaling and spbm-config-mode boot flags, VLANs 3500-3998 are reserved too.


### `vlan members add <vid> <ports> [portmember]`

```
vlan members add 100 1/1-1/24
vlan members remove 1 1/1-1/24
```

On an access port, also remove the port from VLAN 1. Otherwise it stays a member of both VLANs.


### `vlan mlt <vid> <mlt-id>`

```
vlan mlt 100 10
```


### `vlan delete <vid>`

> ▲ **Caution:** Also removes the VLAN's I-SID mapping and IP interface.


### `show vlan members [<vid>] [port <ports>]`

```
show vlan members 100
show vlan members port 1/5
```


### `show lldp neighbor [summary | detail] [port <ports>]`

```
show lldp neighbor summary
show lldp neighbor detail port 1/5
```

Since 9.2 `detail` also shows the chassis ID type and chassis ID.


### `lldp cdp dual-mode-enable`

Up to 9.3, `lldp cdp enable` switches the port to CDP only, so CDP and LLDP could not run together.


### `poe poe-shutdown`

```
interface gigabitEthernet 1/5
poe poe-shutdown
no poe poe-shutdown
```

A remote power-cycle of a hung AP, phone or camera without touching the switch port state.


### `tdr-test port <ports>`

Not supported on all platforms. The link drops briefly during the test.

> ▲ **Caution:** Interrupts traffic on the port for a moment.


### `link-debounce <0-300000>`

```
link-debounce 1000
```

Since 9.4 this cannot be used on Auto-sense ports; use the global `auto-sense link-debounce` there. Show it with `show interfaces gigabitEthernet link-debounce`.


### `mirror-by-port <id> in-port <src-ports> out-port <dst-port> mode <rx | tx | both> enable`

```
mirror-by-port 1 in-port 1/5 out-port 1/48 mode both enable
show mirror-by-port
no mirror-by-port 1
```

Use `monitor-mlt <id>` instead of `out-port` to mirror to an MLT. Remove the mirror when you are done.


### `slpp enable`

```
slpp enable
slpp vid 100
interface gigabitEthernet 1/1-1/24
slpp packet-rx
slpp packet-rx-threshold 5
```

SLPP sends test packets per VLAN, and a port that receives them back is shut down (packet-rx). The receive threshold defaults to 1 and counts all VLANs of a tagged port together. The official values for access-facing SMLT ports of a vIST pair are threshold 5 on the primary and 50 on the secondary peer (so only one side shuts down); do not use packet-rx on core SMLT links. SLPP must be enabled on both vIST peers. Thresholds above 50 risk a high CPU during a loop on busy switches. Also rate-limit broadcast and multicast on access ports.


### `show slpp interface gigabitEthernet [<ports>]`

`show slpp` shows the global settings and VLANs.


### `slpp-guard enable [timeout <0 | 10-65535>]`

Protects against loops built through downstream switches (for example ERS or EXOS stacks). Use it on access switches' access ports, never on NNI uplinks (community guidance). On DvR and Anycast Gateway VLANs, SLPP Guard also recognizes the gateway keep-alive packets, so it detects loops there without SLPP-TX on the VLAN. Check it with `show slpp-guard`.


### `spanning-tree bpduguard enable [timeout <0-65535>]`

The timeout (seconds) re-enables the port automatically; 0 means it stays down. Check it with `show spanning-tree bpduguard`.


### `vlacp enable`

VLACP must also be enabled globally (`vlacp enable` in Global Config). Check it with `show vlacp interface gigabitethernet <ports>`.


### `mac-security limit-learning max-addrs <1-64000>`

```
mac-security limit-learning max-addrs 10
mac-security limit-learning enable
```


### `auto-recover-port port <ports> enable`

Without it, a port that SLPP shut down stays down until someone runs `no shutdown`. Only use it when the loop source is under control, otherwise the port flaps in and out.


### `link-flap-detect auto-port-down / link-flap-detect frequency <n> interval <sec>`

```
link-flap-detect frequency 10
link-flap-detect interval 60
link-flap-detect auto-port-down
```

auto-port-down is off by default (only a trap is sent). Check the settings with `show link-flap-detect`.


### `show spanning-tree mstp status / show spanning-tree mstp port role <ports>`

The fabric core needs no spanning tree, but access switches and SMLT edges still run MSTP. Frequent topology changes flush MAC tables and look like short outages.
